stages.in_text: The retrieved disease records for reflux disease encompass eight distinct clinical entities spanning the gastroesophageal reflux disease spectrum [1][2][3][4][5][6][7][8]. The core condition is Gastroesophageal reflux disease [1], with subtypes that specify the presence or absence of mucosal injury, including Gastroesophageal reflux disease without esophagitis [3] and Gastro-esophageal reflux disease with esophagitis [4]. Additional subtypes capture specific complications, including Gastro-esophageal reflux disease with ulceration [5] and Gastroesophageal reflux disease with apnea [6]. A distinct entity, Alkaline reflux disease [2], and Non-Erosive Reflux Disease [7] further broaden the clinical classification, while History of gastroesophageal reflux disease [8] represents a historical diagnostic category. The MedGen concept titled Gastroesophageal reflux disease [10] anchors the indexing framework, and the literature entity Gastroesophageal Reflux [11] is recognized as an annotated concept in biomedical text. Multiple PubMed publications carry the title Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease [9][14][20], and a related narrative review is titled Gastroesophageal reflux disease and oral health: A narrative review [17], with corresponding PMIDs 29132520 [13], 33351044 [16], and 35605234 [19]. Three ClinicalTrials.gov studies address reflux disease therapeutics, including Famotidine in Subjects With Non-erosive Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease [12], Efficacy of Pantoprazole in Patients Older Than 18 Years Who Have Symptoms of Acid Reflux (Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease) (BY1023/M3-339) [15], and On Demand Treatment of Reflux Disease [18].
